source_text.body:
Scan NASA Lidar data for unmapped Maya sites with parallel agents
A Google engineer pointed 48 AI agents at NASA Lidar data and reportedly found an unmapped Maya pyramid within 72 hours.
·
Nov 11, 2026
Done with a
custom-built or unnamed agent
What they did
After brainstorming with several chatbots, the author created a token on NASA's open lidar portal and had agents convert about 1,200 km² of Maya-region lidar strips into images. 48 agents inspected them against a written guide, with no classifier, and flagged structures. Agents then checked the literature and archives, drafted a Spanish report, and verified the raw point cloud. The author sent the report to INAH.
How it went
One hilltop site with a plaza, an oval pyramid and a possible reservoir appeared unregistered, and INAH's records check found no registered site there. The author says it is not official, and fieldwork is up to INAH.
Worth knowing
The author is not an archaeologist and had to trust the agents' Spanish translation. Any fieldwork needs INAH authorisation, and exact coordinates went in a confidential annex.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
I want to scan public [Lidar dataset, e.g. NASA or USGS Lidar tiles for a region I name] for possible unmapped archaeological features such as [mounds, pyramids, or earthworks]. Split the area into tiles, process them in parallel, and flag candidates by their elevation patterns. Finish with a ranked list of the [10] most promising locations with coordinates, a hillshade image of each, and a note on how confident you are, and be clear these are leads that need expert verification.
Original source: https://pietromiotti.com/latest/maya-site/?maya
